key_insight: Combining atomistic NiAl stiffness with EBSD-informed polycrystal models predicts effective elastic properties in very good agreement with experiment.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports microstructure-aware prediction of NiAl stiffness while accounting for grain orientation and morphology.
method: Compute the cubic single-crystal stiffness tensor using atomistic calculations.
Build an EBSD-informed 3D polycrystal and simulate uniaxial tension with FEM.
Compare effective elastic properties with experiments and analytical homogenization estimates.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports very good FEM–experiment agreement for Young’s modulus and Poisson’s ratio, with minor Young’s modulus deviations for the Hashin–Shtrikman upper bound and self-consistent approximation.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on the atomistic stiffness inputs and microstructure reconstruction; the abstract provides no numerical error metrics.
paper_title: Multiscale evaluation of the elastic response of polycrystalline NiAl using molecular statics, EBSD-based finite element and analytical homogenization methods
